lessons.title: Seed certification and preparing for inspection
lessons.html:
Seed certification and preparing for inspection

Seed certification is a system that gives the buyer confidence that seed is of the variety stated and meets set quality standards. In South Africa, certification schemes run under the Plant Improvement Act and its regulations, and the South African National Seed Organisation (SANSOR) acts as the designated authority for many crop schemes. A seed unit is a defined field or block of a seed crop, for example a hybrid maize seed field or a wheat multiplication block, that is entered for certification.

Why it matters

A farmer who buys certified seed expects the right cultivar, true to type, free of serious off-types and within purity and germination standards. If the seed unit is not inspected properly, a whole season's planting by many farmers can be affected.

Preparing for the inspection

  • Check that the unit was registered with the certification authority before the deadline, with the correct crop, cultivar, class of seed (for example basic or certified) and area.
  • Get the map or GPS coordinates of the unit, the planting date, the parent seed lot labels and the grower's details.
  • Know the standards for that crop and class: required isolation distance from other fields of the same crop, maximum allowed off-types, other crops and specified weeds, and the number of inspections required.
  • Plan the inspection at the right crop stage. For maize hybrid production, flowering is a critical time to check for shedding female plants and off-types.
  • Arrange access with the grower and check that the inspection kit is ready: forms, tally counter, GPS, measuring wheel, sample bags and PPE.

Personal safety

Wear a hat, long sleeves and boots in tall crops. Ask the grower if any spraying was done recently and do not enter a field during its re-entry period on the product label. Carry water and tell someone where you are working.

lessons.title: Inspecting the seed unit
lessons.html:
Inspecting the seed unit

The inspection has two parts: looking at the surroundings and looking inside the unit itself. Both must be recorded.

Surroundings and isolation

  • Walk or drive the boundary. Check neighbouring fields for the same crop or crops that can cross-pollinate.
  • Measure distances where needed. Compare them with the isolation standard for the crop and class.
  • Note sources of contamination such as volunteer plants on road verges, weedy borders or a neighbour's grain maize flowering at the same time.

Inside the unit

  1. Follow the counting pattern in the scheme rules, for example a set number of counts spread in a W or zigzag pattern across the field, so that the whole unit is represented.
  2. At each count, examine the set number of plants and record off-types, other cultivars, other crops and specified weeds.
  3. For hybrids, check male and female rows, detasselling in maize, and any female plants shedding pollen.
  4. Note the general condition: crop health, disease, lodging, pest damage and weeds.

What counts as an off-type?

An off-type is a plant that differs clearly from the description of the cultivar, for example a different height, leaf colour, flower colour, seed colour or maturity. Use the official cultivar description. If you are unsure, compare several plants and ask a senior inspector.

Recording

Write the counts as you go, not from memory afterwards. Record the date, crop stage, weather, and GPS points of problem areas. Photographs help support the report. Calculate the off-type level as the scheme rules describe and compare with the standard.

lessons.title: Concluding the inspection and certifying the unit
lessons.html:
Concluding the inspection and certifying the unit

At the end of the field visit you must decide whether the seed unit meets the standards, needs corrective work, or must be rejected. Your decision is based on facts recorded during the inspection, not on the grower's opinion.

Possible outcomes

OutcomeExample
PassIsolation correct, off-types below the standard
ConditionalOff-types slightly high; grower must rogue (remove) them and the unit is re-inspected
Partial rejectionA border strip near a contaminating field is excluded from certification
RejectionIsolation failure that cannot be fixed, or contamination far above standard

Concluding with the grower

  • Discuss the findings with the grower or farm manager before you leave. Show them problem areas.
  • Explain any corrective action needed, such as roguing off-types, cutting out a border, or detasselling, and the date for re-inspection.
  • Stay professional. A grower may be under financial pressure, but the standards apply to everyone.

Completing certification

  1. Complete the inspection report fully and sign it.
  2. Submit it to the certification authority within the time required.
  3. Record re-inspection results when they are done.
  4. When the unit passes all field inspections, the harvested seed can move to processing. It must still pass laboratory tests for purity and germination before certified labels are issued for the seed lots.
  5. File copies of all reports for the period your procedure requires.

Integrity

Never sign a report for a field you did not inspect, and never accept gifts to change a result. Certification depends on trust.

Key points

  • Certification confirms variety identity and quality standards for buyers.
  • Prepare with registration details, standards and the right crop stage.
  • Check isolation and count off-types using the official pattern.
  • Decisions are pass, conditional, partial rejection or rejection, based on recorded facts.
  • Field approval is followed by laboratory testing before seed is labelled.

quiz.question: What does seed certification give the buyer?

options.text: Confidence the seed is of the stated variety and meets standards
A plant that differs clearly from the cultivar description
A plant with a pest on it
A plant on the edge of the field

quiz.question: Why are counts spread in a W or zigzag pattern?

options.text: So the whole unit is represented

options.text: Conditional: rogue the off-types and re-inspect

options.text: The seed must pass laboratory purity and germination tests
